subject: Post-call: SLO targets, streaming/concurrency clarifications and harness artifacts
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: SLO targets, streaming/concurrency clarifications and harness artifacts

Oliver — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps so we have a concrete handoff for the performance qualification lab run.

High-level agreement from the call
- Target latency (non-streaming): p50 <= 40ms, p95 <= 150ms, p99 <= 350ms for single-shot generative calls (~150 tokens output)
- Streaming requirements: first-chunk (initial byte) <= 100ms, per-chunk latency <= 35ms for subsequent frames; progressive output must not exceed 200ms between chunks for the user-facing stream
- Throughput & concurrency: target sustained throughput = 120 req/s across the workload mix; target concurrency = 32 active concurrent requests (streams count towards concurrency)
- Cold vs warm: we agreed to benchmark both cold-start (empty KV/cache) and warm (pre-populated KV for the prompt prefixes used).

Deliverables we'll provide by EOD tomorrow (Dec 2):
- Redwood harness template (attached) with exact CLI flags we’ll use to reproduce runs
- Prompt set samples (attached) and mapping to EdgeCommerce intents
- Measurement definitions doc (latency percentiles, how we sample tokens, error handling)

Proposed schedule
- Dec 7: calibration run and quick validation with your load profile
- Dec 8: three measurement windows (warm) + one cold run if you want cold data

Open questions for EdgeCommerce (please confirm):
1) Will the benchmark run against your production-like dataset or a sanitized subset?
2) For streaming, are you expecting our per-chunk numbers to include network overhead on your side, or should we measure from model process -> client SDK (we typically measure at the SDK boundary unless you want a network-included SLA)
3) Do you have a preferred monitoring/ingestion endpoint for per-token traces (e.g., a temporary Prometheus pushgateway or a S3/Drive location)?

Attachments: redwood-harness-template.yaml (text), prompt-sample-sets.zip (zip)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the harness runbook and a reproducibility checklist.

—
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@edgecommerce.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO targets, streaming/concurrency clarifications and harness artifacts

Thanks David — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Dataset: we'll run against a production-like, sanitized subset that mirrors our 3 intent buckets (checkout, search, recommendation). I'll attach the load profile CSV so you can map the mix.
2) Network inclusion: we'd prefer end-to-end numbers that include our network (client -> model). However, for debugging it's useful to have both SDK-boundary numbers and client-included numbers. Can you provide both or at least guidance on what the delta typically is?
3) Burst behavior: one of our concerns is tail latency when bursts happen (10x baseline for 30s). Will your harness support a burst window?

Preferred test window: Dec 7 (calibration) and Dec 8 (measurement). We can make afternoons available PST.

Attached: edge-load-profile.csv (CSV) — this has request mix and example payload sizes.

On the list of deliverables, can you also include a minimal reproducibility checklist (what artifacts we should capture and how to store them) and a short mapping of Redwood model variants to fallback tiers (e.g., fast-approx -> low-cost fallback) so we can review risk?

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 03 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO targets, streaming/concurrency clarifications and harness artifacts

Oliver — tagging in a few measurement specifics and the reproducibility checklist we discussed on the call.

Measurement definitions (we will publish these verbatim in the harness repo):
- Latency measurement window: measure from SDK send() to SDK receive() (two metrics) and also capture model-process-to-first-byte for internal debugging. Record p50/p90/p95/p99 and sample raw distribution.
- Streaming: define "first-byte" as time from SDK send() to arrival of the first chunk; "inter-chunk" as time between consecutive onNext()/chunk events at the SDK. We'll compute per-chunk p95 as well as a session-level max inter-chunk.
- Concurrency: active requests at any instant. For streams, concurrency counts while the stream is open. We will report concurrent open streams and concurrent non-stream requests separately.
- Warm vs cold: cold = empty KV and no prior model cache; warm = run a single pre-population pass with 10% of traffic weight for 5 minutes, then run measurement windows.
- Burst test: we will run a 30s 10x ramp followed by stabilization windows; we will capture tail latency during the ramp and 60s after the ramp.

Repro checklist (attached repro-checklist.md) — highlights:
- Container image digest (sha256) for the runtime and model server
- Harness CLI command and config file (we'll provide redwood-harness-template.yaml)
- Prompt set and seed mapping (we'll provide prompt-sample-sets.zip)
- Load profile CSV with timestamps and mix (Edge provided)
- Raw telemetry export (perf traces, token counts, and model logs) and a produced summary CSV
- Tagged run IDs and upload location (Drive path provided below)

Run plan:
1) Calibration (Dec 7): validate environment, verify pre-population script, run a short 5-min smoke at low concurrency.
2) Measurement (Dec 8): three 10-minute measurement windows (warm) separated by 5-minute cool-downs + one cold run at the end. We will record full telemetry for each window.

Artifacts we'll hand off after each measurement window:
- Full run manifest (CLI, config, image digest)
- Run tarball (logs + telemetry) stored at the Drive folder
- Summary CSV with p50/p90/p95/p99 and throughput figures

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-redwood-ec-bench
Attachments: repro-checklist.md (text), harness-runbook.pdf (pdf)

Let us know if you want our team to also publish SDK-side aggregated numbers vs client-included numbers. We can do both; it just adds one extra telemetry sink to the run.

—
Monica Patel
Performance PM, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
